title: Fordham Edge partner recon + outbound sketch
body:
ONE-LINE: Fordham Edge (mid-market logistics SaaS) — potential pilot for private inference + embeddings for route optimization assistant. Price-sensitive; cares about latency in EMEA; security checklist heavy.

Quick snapshot:
- Company: Fordham Edge (faux name for target). Logistics planning platform for regional carriers, 200–800 employees, HQ London + regional offices in Paris/Frankfurt.
- What they do: scheduling, dynamic routing, delivery ETAs, carrier marketplace. Heavy near-real-time inference use in route optimization and ETA; currently evaling embedding-based similarity for historical route recall and a chat support agent for dispatchers.
- Why Redwood might win: unified offering across hosted->private (they care about PII and EU residency), cost controls (token/op economics matter for high volume), and routing/fallback for reliability.

Product fit & hypothesis:
- Primary use case: embeddings-powered search over historical delivery logs + light generation for dispatcher assistant (form-fill suggestions, SLA reminders).
- Secondary: reranking candidate routes, short-form explanation generation for drivers (SMS-friendly).
- Need: sub-200ms tail latency for dispatcher flows (low token budgets per query), on-prem or VPC-hosted inference to meet data residency and audit requirements.
- Opportunity: Redwood Dedicated or Private plus Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) to hit cost targets.

Integration surface / technical notes (raw):
- Current infra: AWS EU regions, some on-prem in warehouses; central Postgres + S3 logs, Kafka for eventing.
- Likely integration: embeddings service for search (periodic batch indexing), streaming chat for dispatcher UI, and an offline reranker endpoint for candidate routes.
- Auth: want SSO + API key rotation + KMS for keys. KMS/HSM requirement flagged by legal.
- Preview constraints: 8k context for some workflows; in long-term maybe need multi-chunk retrieval.

Key stakeholders (names mined from LinkedIn / docs):
- VP Product: Claire Dubois (primary decision maker for product fit).
- Head of Data Science: Tomás Alvarez (careful about model accuracy and drift).
- CTO / Infra Lead: Markus Heinemann (security, deployment model).
- Procurement / Legal contact: Sophie Laurent (SLA / KMS / data processing terms).

KPIs they care about:
- Mean time to suggestion (should be < 200ms interactive).
- Cost per query (target <$0.005 per inference for high-volume embed+rerank path).
- False positive rate for route picks (safety/regression metric).
- Auditability: token logs + model versioning + eval hooks.

Pricing sensitivity & contract signals:
- Startups they bought from: prefer monthly/annual committed capacity to manage costs.
- Procurement historically negotiates tight caps on overages and wants predictable unit economics.
- Will likely require a pilot first; procurement only enters for >$50k ARR.

Pain points we can call out in outreach:
- Current embeddings are slow and inconsistent across regions; search quality drift after peak loads.
- Dev time to port to private stack has been a blocker for Sec/Legal signoff.
- Unclear fallback when primary model unavailable, leads to SLA misses.

Draft outbound email (subject lines to test):
- Subject A: Quick idea for sub-200ms dispatcher suggestions at Fordham Edge
- Subject B: Reduce route-search cost and keep data in your EU VPC

Email body (short, cold prospecting):
Hi Claire —
I was looking at Fordham Edge's routing product and noticed you’re surfacing historical route matches and real-time dispatcher suggestions. We’ve helped logistics platforms cut inference cost by ~6x through batching + KV caching while enabling private deployments that keep data in customer VPCs.
Would you be open to a 20-min pilot plan where we benchmark a single dispatcher flow (EU region, 200ms tail target) and show estimated unit-costs? I can bring an engineer to walk through security and a brief MPT.
— Maya

LinkedIn / DM variant (short):
Hi Claire — I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference. Short question: would you be open to a 20-min tech review on embeddings latency and privacy options for Fordham Edge?

Call / discovery script (bullet-y):
1) Quick intros (2 min) — who’s on the call and top constraint (latency, cost, compliance)?
2) Confirm current infra and flows — what hits the dispatcher UI now? tokens, qps, tail latency? (ask for numbers)
3) Share 1-2 Redwood patterns — Dedicated GPU pool + KV caching for embeddings, VPC Private installs, and model fallbacks.
4) Agree a pilot scope — single dispatcher route suggestion flow + 2-week perf + cost baseline.
5) Next steps — engineer-to-engineer kickoff, security questionnaire, and procurement touchpoint.

Objections we should be ready with + suggested replies (raw):
- \"We can't open data to a vendor.\" => Reply: we can run Private (customer-managed control plane + VPC) or on-prem; keys remain in your KMS/HSM and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
- \"Cost is unknown / vendor lock-in.\" => Reply: pilot includes unit-cost baseline and a migration plan; Redwood supports model export paths and exposes model variant control so you aren’t forced into one SKU.
- \"Latency targets are unrealistic / can't hit 200ms.\" => Reply: many customers hit sub-200ms with a combined approach (smaller model routing, continuous batching, prefix caching); propose a micro-benchmark as first step.
- \"We already have embeddings infra.\" => Reply: ask about tail latency and recall quality; show comparative eval on small sample (we can run 1000 queries and show precision/recall delta).

Open questions / info to collect during discovery:
- Current QPS and 95/99 tail latency numbers for dispatcher UI (EU region).
- Typical token length for generator prompts in dispatcher flows.
- Legal: list of data types touching PII; KMS / HSM vendor preferences.
- Is there a preferred procurement threshold and timeline for pilots?

Pilot plan (two-week outline):
- Week 0 (prep): NDA + security questionnaire + sample dataset selection (1000 historical routes sanitized).
- Week 1: baseline measurement on customer's current stack (latency, cost, recall), Redwood test deployment with same dataset (embeddings + a small chat model), collect metrics.
- Week 2: optimize (quantization, batch windows, cache hotpaths), present results + recommended Dedicated/Private configuration + cost model.

To-dos (mine / team):
- Arjun: draft short SOW for two-week pilot (due 2025-03-07).
- Maya: reach out to Claire on LinkedIn with Subject A and follow-up email template.
- Riley: pull quick benchmark script for 1k embeddings queries to run against public benchmarks (due 2025-02-20).
- Security: draft one-pager on KMS/HSM support and audit logs to attach to pilot invite.

Raw scratch / quick mental notes (unordered):
- Potential hook: \"route memory\" demo button in product to show embeddings recall quality — quick wins in UX.
- If procurement stalls, propose a 30-day paid PoC with limited commit to buy down legal risk.
- Watch out for regional cloud partner resellers in EU (might prefer a regional partner for Private installs).

End of notes — will iterate this after the first outreach and initial discovery.
